questions.question: A train of length 282 m takes 12 seconds to pass over another train 248 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 68 km/hr, then find the speed of the second train.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 282 + 248 = 530 m

Relative speed = 530 ÷ 12 ≈ 44.17 m/s

Convert first train speed: 68 km/hr = 18.89 m/s

Second train speed = 44.17 − 18.89 ≈ 25.28 m/s

**∴ Answer = 91 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train = 282 m

Length of second train = 248 m

Time = 12 seconds

Speed of first train = 68 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Relative speed (opposite direction) = (sum of lengths) ÷ time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 282 + 248 = 530 m

⇒ Relative speed = 530 ÷ 12 ≈ 44.17 m/s

⇒ Convert 68 km/hr into m/s ⇒ 68 × 5/18 ≈ 18.89 m/s

⇒ Let speed of second train = v

⇒ Relative speed = 18.89 + v

⇒ 18.89 + v = 44.17

⇒ v ≈ 25.28 m/s

⇒ Convert into km/hr ⇒ 25.28 × 18/5 ≈ 91 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 91 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds are added.

Train Crossing Rule

Distance = sum of lengths when crossing.

Unit Conversion

km/hr to m/s ⇒ multiply by 5/18.

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,000 at 7% per annum rate of interest for the period from 5 February 2023 to 19 April 2023.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total days from 5 Feb to 19 Apr = 23 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 19 (Apr) = 73 days.

Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years.

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

SI = (2000 × 7 × 1/5) ÷ 100 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 
 5 Feb 2023
 P = ₹2000
 19 Apr 2023
 SI = ₹28
 

 Time = 73 Days (1/5 Year)
 Rate = 7% p.a.

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 7% per annum

Time Period = 5 February 2023 to 19 April 2023

**Time Calculation:**

⇒ Year 2023 is a non-leap year, so February has 28 days.

⇒ Days in February (28 − 5) = 23 days

⇒ Days in March = 31 days

⇒ Days in April = 19 days

⇒ Total Time in days = 23 + 31 + 19 = 73 days

⇒ Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = [2000 × 7 × (1/5)] ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2000 × 7) ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 14000 ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 28

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number of Days Calculation Trick

In standard exam interest calculations, either the deposit day or the withdrawal day is counted, but not both. Total days generally sum up to a multiple of 73 (as 365 ÷ 73 = 5). Thus, keep in mind: 73 days = 1/5 year, 146 days = 2/5 year, and 219 days = 3/5 year.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated consistently only on the principal amount over the given duration. Conversely, Compound Interest recalculates interest on both the principal and the previously accumulated interest.

Leap Year Identification

Always verify the year. A year completely divisible by 4 is a leap year (having 29 days in February). For century years (like 1900, 2000), they must be divisible by 400 to be classified as leap years.

questions.question: If m and n are positive integers and (m – n) is an even number, then (m² – n²) will always be divisible by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

m − n even ⇒ m and n have same parity (both even or both odd)

Then m + n is also even

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

Even × Even = divisible by 4

**∴ Answer = 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

m − n is even

**Formula used:**

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

**Calculation:**

⇒ If m − n is even ⇒ m and n are both even or both odd

⇒ Case 1: m, n both even ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ Case 2: m, n both odd ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ So in all cases, both factors are even

⇒ Product = even × even

⇒ Hence divisible by 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

Parity Concept

Same parity numbers give even sum and difference.

Divisibility Rule

Product of two even numbers is always divisible by 4.

questions.question: In a right – angled ABC, right – angled at B, if tanA = (3)/(4), then find cosec A.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given tan A = 3/4, which represents the ratio of Perpendicular to Base.

The sides form a standard Pythagorean triplet of (3, 4, 5).

Thus, Perpendicular = 3, Base = 4, and Hypotenuse = 5.

We know that cosec A = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular.

⇒ cosec A = 5/3

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In a right-angled ΔABC, right-angled at B, tan A = 3/4

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

cosec A = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular

 
 
 
 A A B C Base = 4x Perp = 3x Hypotenuse = 5x 

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan A = BC / AB = 3 / 4

⇒ Let Perpendicular BC = 3x and Base AB = 4x.

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem in ΔABC:

⇒ AC² = AB² + BC²

⇒ AC² = (4x)² + (3x)²

⇒ AC² = 16x² + 9x²

⇒ AC² = 25x²

⇒ AC = √(25x²) = 5x

⇒ Now, cosec A = AC / BC

⇒ cosec A = 5x / 3x = 5/3

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse | tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard integer combinations fulfilling the Pythagoras theorem include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Reciprocal Identities

cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ | sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ | cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

questions.question: The mode of the observations 9, 6, 8, 1, 9, 6, 4, 5, 7, 1, 6, 5, 3, 6, 6, 3 and 3 is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mode is simply the observation that appears the maximum number of times in a given dataset.

By quickly scanning the numbers: 9, 6, 8, 1, 9, 6, 4, 5, 7, 1, 6, 5, 3, 6, 6, 3, 3

We can easily see that the number 6 appears most frequently (a total of 5 times).

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**Given:**

Observations = 9, 6, 8, 1, 9, 6, 4, 5, 7, 1, 6, 5, 3, 6, 6, 3, 3

**Formula Used:**

Mode = The value with the highest frequency in a given set of data.

 Frequency Distribution

**Calculations:**

⇒ Frequency of 1 = 2

Mean

The mean is the arithmetic average of all observations, calculated as the sum of all values divided by the total number of values.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when the data set is arranged in ascending or descending order. For an even number of observations, it is the average of the two central values.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Bimodal and Multimodal Datasets

A dataset can have more than one mode. If two different numbers share the highest frequency, the dataset is called bimodal. If more than two numbers share the highest frequency, it is multimodal.

questions.question: ₹10,415 is divided among P, Q, and R in such a way that if ₹62, ₹17, and ₹79 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 15:10:14. Find the difference between the original shares of Q and R.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

After deduction ⇒ ratio = 15 : 10 : 14

Let shares = 15x, 10x, 14x

Original total ⇒ (15x+62)+(10x+17)+(14x+79)=10415

⇒ 39x + 158 = 10415 ⇒ x = 263

**∴ Difference = (14x+79) − (10x+17) = 1114**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = 10415

Deductions: P = 62, Q = 17, R = 79

Ratio after deduction = 15 : 10 : 14

**Formula used:**

If quantities are in ratio a : b : c ⇒ values = ax, bx, cx

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let reduced shares be 15x, 10x, 14x

⇒ Original shares: P = 15x + 62, Q = 10x + 17, R = 14x + 79

⇒ Sum = (15x + 62) + (10x + 17) + (14x + 79) = 10415

⇒ 39x + 158 = 10415

⇒ 39x = 10257

⇒ x = 263

⇒ Q = 10x + 17 = 2647

⇒ R = 14x + 79 = 3761

⇒ Difference = 3761 − 2647 = 1114

**∴ The correct answer is 1114.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Adjusted Ratio Method

Assume ratio after deduction, then add constants back.

Linear Equation

Use total sum to find x.

Difference Shortcut

Difference = (ratio difference × x) adjusted with constants.

questions.question: The number of diagonals of an n-sided regular polygon is 665. What is the value of ‘n’?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use formula: diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

Given = 665 ⇒ n(n − 3) = 1330

Check nearby values ⇒ 38 × 35 = 1330

So n = 38

**∴ Answer = 38**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of diagonals = 665

**Formula used:**

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 665

⇒ n(n − 3) = 1330

⇒ n² − 3n − 1330 = 0

⇒ n² − 38n + 35n − 1330 = 0

⇒ n(n − 38) + 35(n − 38) = 0

⇒ (n + 35)(n − 38) = 0

⇒ n = 38 (positive value)

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal Formula

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

Quadratic Formation

Rearrange equation into standard quadratic form.

Factorization

Split middle term to solve quadratic easily.

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 12 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 24 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 12 and 24 = 24 units.

Combined efficiency of P and Q = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 units/hr.

Efficiency of P = 24 ÷ 24 = 1 unit/hr.

Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr.

Time for Q to fill 1/4th of the cistern = (24 ÷ 4) ÷ 1 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together = 12 hours

Time taken by P alone = 24 hours

 
 

 **Person**

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = 24 units

⇒ Work required to fill one-fourth of the cistern = 24 × (1/4) = 6 units

⇒ Time taken by Q = Work required ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q = 6 ÷ 1 = 6 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work (Emptying Pipes)

If a pipe or leak empties a tank, its efficiency is taken as negative. Net efficiency = Sum of filling efficiency − Sum of emptying efficiency.

Capacity of Cistern

Total Capacity = Time taken to fill or empty the tank × Rate of water flow (in liters/hour or similar units).

Alternating Pipes

When pipes are opened in alternate hours, calculate the combined work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 hours), multiply it to get closest to total work, and then calculate the remaining work for the next respective pipe.
</p

questions.question: Five years ago, Meera was three times as old as her niece, Kavya. Seven years from now, Meera will be twice as old as Kavya. What is Meera’s current age (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let present ages be M and K

5 years ago: M − 5 = 3(K − 5)

7 years later: M + 7 = 2(K + 7)

Solving quickly ⇒ K = 17, M = 41

**∴ Answer = 41 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let present age of Meera = M

Let present age of Kavya = K

5 years ago: M − 5 = 3 × (K − 5)

7 years from now: M + 7 = 2 × (K + 7)

**Formula used:**

Linear equations: solve simultaneous equations

**Calculation:**

⇒ M − 5 = 3K − 15

⇒ M = 3K − 10

⇒ M + 7 = 2K + 14

⇒ M = 2K + 7

⇒ 3K − 10 = 2K + 7

⇒ K = 17

⇒ M = 2K + 7 = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Equation Concept

Translate time-based conditions into equations.

Simultaneous Equations

Solve equations to determine unknown ages.

Verification

Check values satisfy both given conditions.

questions.question: An item with a marked price of ₹657 was sold for ₹526. What was the percentage of discount given? (Round off the answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 657 − 526 = 131

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (131 ÷ 657) × 100

We know that 20% of 657 is 131.4, which is very close to 131.

Since 131 is slightly less than 131.4 (by 0.4), the percentage will be slightly less than 20%.

0.4 is about 0.06% of 657. So, 20% − 0.06% = 19.94%.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.94%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹657

Selling Price (SP) = ₹526

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 
 MP = ₹657
 
 
 SP = ₹526
 
 

 

 Discount = ₹131
 
 Discount % = (131 ÷ 657) × 100 ≈ 19.94%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 657 − 526 = 131

⇒ Discount % = (131 ÷ 657) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 13100 ÷ 657

⇒ Discount % = 19.9391...

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 19.94%.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.94%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The printed or labeled price on an article. Any discount offered by a seller is always calculated on the Marked Price, not the Cost Price.

Selling Price (SP)

The final price at which a product is sold after deducting the discount. Formula: SP = MP × (1 − Discount / 100).

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are offered sequentially, they are called successive discounts. For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by: (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: The average of 13 numbers is 7. If each number is multiplied by 3, then what will the new average be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each observation of a given dataset is multiplied by a constant k, the new average is equal to the original average multiplied by k.

Given original average = 7

Since each number is multiplied by 3, the new average will be 7 × 3.

New average = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of observations = 13

Original average = 7

 
 13 Numbers
 Average = 7
 
 
• 
 

 × 3
 
 
 New Dataset
 Average = 21
 
 Average scales directly with all elements

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Total number of observations

New Average = New Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original sum of the 13 numbers = 7 × 13 = 91

⇒ If each individual number is multiplied by 3, the total sum also gets multiplied by 3.

⇒ New sum of the 13 numbers = 91 × 3 = 273

⇒ New Average = 273 ÷ 13

⇒ New Average = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition / Subtraction Rule in Averages

If a constant value 'c' is added to or subtracted from every observation of a dataset, the new average will be the old average plus or minus 'c'.

Multiplication / Division Rule in Averages

If each observation of a dataset is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average will be the old average multiplied or divided by 'k'.

Combined Average

For two distinct groups with sample sizes n₁ and n₂ and averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, the combined average is calculated as (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: A seller makes a loss of 5% by selling a shirt for ₹1,000. He would have made x% profit by selling for ₹1,400. Find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss 5% ⇒ SP = 95% of CP

1000 = 0.95 × CP ⇒ CP = 1000 ÷ 0.95 = 1052.63

Profit at 1400 = 1400 − 1052.63 = 347.37

Profit % = (347.37 / 1052.63) × 100 ≈ 33%

**∴ Answer = 33%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss = 5%, SP₁ = 1000

New SP₂ = 1400

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 − loss%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP₁ = CP × 0.95

⇒ 1000 = 0.95 × CP

⇒ CP = 1000 ÷ 0.95 = 1052.63

⇒ Profit = 1400 − 1052.63 = 347.37

⇒ Profit% = (347.37 ÷ 1052.63) × 100 ≈ 33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

SP = CP × (1 − loss%)

Profit Formula

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Mohan and David, are in the ratio 5 : 8, respectively, and each of them saves ₹75,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 4, find the monthly income of Mohan(in ₹).
questions.solution:

Income ratio = 5 : 8 ⇒ incomes = 5x, 8x

Saving same ⇒ difference in income = difference in expenditure

⇒ 8x − 5x = 4y − y ⇒ 3x = 3y ⇒ x = y

Now saving = income − expenditure

⇒ 5x − x = 75000 ⇒ 4x = 75000 ⇒ x = 18750

Mohan’s income = 5x = 93750

**∴ Answer = ₹93750**

⇒ Let expenditures be y and 4y

⇒ For David: 8x − 4y = 75000

⇒ Subtract equations:

⇒ (8x − 4y) − (5x − y) = 0

⇒ 3x − 3y = 0 ⇒ x = y

⇒ Substitute in first equation:

⇒ 5x − x = 75000

⇒ 4x = 75000

⇒ x = 18750

⇒ Mohan’s income = 5x = 93750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹93750.**

questions.question: A cistern has two inlet pipes, A and B, and one outlet pipe, C. Pipe A can fill the cistern alone in 15 hours, pipe B in 18 hours, and pipe C can empty it in 27 hours. For the first 5 hours, pipes A and B are opened together. Then, for the next 12 hours, pipes B and C are opened together. After that, only pipe B works. How long will pipe B alone take to fill the remaining part of the cistern?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM of 15, 18, 27 = 270 units.

Efficiency: A = +18, B = +15, C = −10.

Work by (A + B) in 5 hrs = (18 + 15) × 5 = 165 units.

Work by (B + C) in 12 hrs = (15 − 10) × 12 = 60 units.

Remaining work = 270 − (165 + 60) = 45 units.

Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 18 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to empty the cistern = 27 hours

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times taken by the pipes.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

For an emptying pipe, the efficiency is taken as negative.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pipe A (+)
 15
 270
 18
 
 

 Pipe B (+)
 18
 15
 
 

 Pipe C (−)
 27
 −10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipes A and B = 18 + 15 = 33 units/hr

⇒ Work done by A and B in the first 5 hours = 33 × 5 = 165 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipes B and C = 15 + (−10) = 5 units/hr

⇒ Work done by B and C in the next 12 hours = 5 × 12 = 60 units

⇒ Total work done so far = 165 + 60 = 225 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 270 − 225 = 45 units

⇒ Time taken by Pipe B alone to finish the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency +), whereas an outlet pipe empties it (negative efficiency −). The net rate is the algebraic sum of their individual rates.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, not simply by their daily efficiency unless they work for the exact same number of days.

Alternate Working Hours

When pipes operate alternately, calculate the net work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 hours). Multiply the cycle to reach as close to total work without exceeding it, then manually add remaining work.

questions.question:
Simplify:
 [(3x + 5y)² - 60xy] div [(3x - 5y)²]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the direct algebraic identity: (a + b)² − 4ab = (a − b)².

Here, let a = 3x and b = 5y. Then 4ab = 4 × 3x × 5y = 60xy.

The numerator directly simplifies to: (3x + 5y)² − 60xy = (3x − 5y)².

Dividing the numerator by the identical denominator gives: (3x − 5y)² ÷ (3x − 5y)² = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: [(3x + 5y)² − 60xy] ÷ [(3x − 5y)²]

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, expand the terms inside the numerator: [(3x)² + (5y)² + 2 × 3x × 5y − 60xy] ÷ [(3x − 5y)²]

⇒ [9x² + 25y² + 30xy − 60xy] ÷ [(3x − 5y)²]

⇒ Subtract the like terms in the numerator: [9x² + 25y² − 30xy] ÷ [(3x − 5y)²]

⇒ Notice that the expression in the numerator perfectly matches the expanded form of (3x − 5y)²

⇒ Substitute it back: [(3x − 5y)²] ÷ [(3x − 5y)²]

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

Important Application

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab, which directly links the sums, differences, and products of two variables.
